text.holders.staked.info:
{ticker} locked in Zebec SuperApp staking: the raw sum of every unclaimed on-chain staking position (~4.75B at the 2026-10-28 scan). Shown separately from Retail Held — staked is not merged into the retail holder total for this project.

Disclaimer — Super App "Global Staked" is not current TVL: Zebec's Super App shows a much larger "Global Staked" figure (~18.9B) that appears to sum each lockup's cumulative totalStaked counter, not live unclaimed positions. This site's Staked tile is live TVL — the sum of unclaimed UserStakeData positions (~4.75B). Open the (i) methodology tip on Staking Overview for Solscan links to the staking program, lockups, and stake vaults so you can verify both numbers on-chain.

Two staking totals on this site, both intentional: the Supply view's Staking bucket is slightly larger (~4.76B) because it counts what the staking program's vault accounts hold — the stake vaults plus two reward vaults (undistributed rewards, which are nobody's stake). This tile counts stakers' positions instead. The small difference is those reward vaults minus the ZBCN Lockup gap below; it is not a counting error.

ZBCN Lockup vault gap (2.42%): this one lockup (AYbW5cbZEUgLEj6Eiy3yg74PU3YbEHkbFxgW6fjbSJjp) is exempt from our 0.5% position-vs-vault reconcile check. Its unclaimed positions add up to ~2.42% (~4.39M {ticker}) more than its stake-vault token account (ATA) currently holds. Published staked figures use the raw position sums as-is (not scaled down to the vault balance); the vault ATA balance is listed in the Supply view's Staking bucket for transparency.
text.staking.intro: {ticker} staked in Zebec SuperApp staking, summed from unclaimed on-chain positions and counted once per staker. The Supply view's Staking bucket reads slightly higher because it counts vault balances, including reward vaults.
text.supply.staking.description: {ticker} held by Zebec SuperApp staking vault accounts: the per-lockup stake vaults plus two reward vaults (undistributed rewards). Counted by vault token balance, so it differs slightly from the Holders Staked tile, which sums stakers' positions — both figures are intentional. Zebec Super App "Global Staked" (~18.9B) is a different, cumulative-looking metric and is not this vault TVL.
text.supply.residual.title: Below the {supply} max (buybacks / burns)
text.supply.residual.body: The ~{gap} gap between the fixed {total} max supply and every {ticker} balance we count on Solana. {name} keeps a fixed {supply} max while buybacks and burns shrink the on-chain supply, so this is a reconcile note — on-chain supply sitting slightly under the max — not missing wallets and not tokens in a bridge ({ticker} here is Solana-only).
text.supply.residual.note: Counted wallets add up to the mint's current on-chain supply; the shortfall to {total} is consistent with buybacks/burns (not itemised burn-by-burn here). Recomputed on every refresh.
text.supply.holdings.description: Zebec team cluster ({amount} {ticker}): signer wallets of the Zebec multisigs that control the buyback treasury and the three large treasury vaults. Only the ops/payout wallet currently holds {ticker}; the other signers are tagged for completeness. Identified from on-chain multisig ownership (no public Zebec doc names them).

staking.how: Staked {ticker} is the live sum of every unclaimed UserStakeData position on Zebec SuperApp staking (program zSTKzGLiN6T6EVzhBiL6sjULXMahDavAS2p4R62afGv), counted once per staker (~4.75B). It is shown separately from Retail Held for this project (not merged into the retail total). Zebec Super App's "Global Staked" (~18.9B) is a different metric — it tracks each lockup's cumulative totalStaked counter and is not current TVL; do not treat it as the live staked amount.
staking.verify: Open the staking program and each lockup / stake-vault ATA on Solscan. Live TVL matches the sum of unclaimed positions (~4.75B); summing lockup totalStaked counters reproduces the larger Super App-style figure (~18.9B).

supplyBreakdown.how: Total supply is the fixed {supply} max. We split it into simple buckets — retail wallets, staking vaults, project treasury, and a small gap below the max — so the pieces add to {supply}. Each bucket is built from on-chain Solana token-account balances of labelled addresses; the gap below the max reflects buybacks/burns shrinking on-chain supply, not bridges (ZBCN is Solana-only here).

supply.definition: The fixed {ticker} max supply ({supply}). {ticker} is tracked on Solana only; buybacks and burns shrink the on-chain supply slightly below the max, shown on the Supply view as a reconcile gap.

pipelineNotes.cexWallets: 2026-10-25: 44 Solana CEX/custody wallets in config/projects/zebec-network/cex-wallets.json — 11 owner-approved from the Dune spellbook cex_solana_addresses intersect, plus 33 Solscan name-tag-confirmed (Uphold, Crypto.com, Kraken, OKX, Gate, CoinSpot, Bitget, MEXC, KuCoin, Bitrue, Bitvavo, BingX, Bitunix, CoinDCX Fireblocks, Fireblocks Custody) applied under the owner explorer-confirmed auto-apply rule (docs/zbcn-wallet-candidates.md §3). UPHOLD CAVEAT: Zebec says buybacks are consolidated periodically with Uphold Institutional for custody (x.com/Zebec_HQ/status/2112911986245910804; zebec.io/blog/inside-the-zbcn-buyback-program), so part of the Uphold Hot Wallet 3/5 balances (~20.55B + ~128.6M) may be project custodial buybacks; it cannot be split on-chain and is counted as cex. Fireblocks Custody (Fcmiy/4yqgc/FxmR1) owner is unknown; classed cex as institutional custody. Scheduled sync still needs its own pipeline.duneCexQueryId (Solana query on cex.addresses WHERE blockchain=solana; never TEL 3761086).
pipelineNotes.treasuryTeam: 2026-10-26 owner-approved: contracts{} treasury vaults H8Hr964ApEP3ie1rwRTT7wkSrgvUqJQb8oNAKspkDDfR, 3J7n5Usmei8BqgUHan5xuBiJkAx6M1AQQhGwbKiVdQ17, 71LxiE4PvxdZxLmtGcoKAJEWKofPqYw5Wdn6PSpXHodV (role treasury, medium confidence: on-chain multisig overlap with EkXEg; no public doc names them) and team cluster (role holdings → Team Wallets). These seven wallets are the owners (signers) of four Zebec multisigs (program b6ZPysThkApNx2YDiGsPUiYPE7Ub1kTRdCWp7gBkzbr). One controls the officially published buyback treasury EkXEg6de172aoLvr7w86YzQ2rf5oEFD3iUt8uQsLQuQW; the other three control vaults H8Hr, 3J7n5, and 71LxiE (each vault is the signer PDA of its multisig; owner sets overlap). ZBCN moves between the vaults and these signers. Additionally, 9Sq2 signed MintAdmin on 2024-08-26 (program GaK9kh…) and minted 1.6B ZBCN via mint authority 8r8Qgw… — only a project admin key can do that (txs 4acjHJWHmsYNzAdrddjeGJqYQHCCG5GC2FZehgq4pYvcgkvrixbqKjVDLAHcWNodx7baFWZbQ6mPfFVKB1MbSC9a and 42j2ms2HTw2sSCGc5nmwAivrWaRmhcLr1LC6fbmP41DJfv9KT8kHsGwVT62qLu3gBWCGNdbtzs7QVYHk462P2G9t). Confidence: high for 9Sq2; medium for the rest; low for 9jRR (one multisig only). No public Zebec doc names these wallets. Excluded (still candidates): GXD2, 43wqg, 56veX. Evidence: docs/zbcn-wallet-candidates.md §1; official buyback seed https://x.com/Zebec_HQ/status/2112911986245910804.
